speaker: Doctor
text: That is an interesting start; please describe the nature and timing of your pruritus, specifically if it worsens at night or after eating fatty foods. Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your urine color, stool consistency, or the appearance of your skin or eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you experienced any jaundice, dark urine, or clay-colored stools recently? Given your history of ulcerative colitis and high-risk sexual behavior, we also need to rule out sexually transmitted infections; have you noticed any penile or anal lesions, or flu-like symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Liver panel (AST, ALT, ALP, Bilirubin, GGT), RPR/VDRL, HIV 1/2, Hepatitis A/B/C serologies.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Panel: AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L, Alkaline Phosphatase 460 U/L, Bilirubin Total 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin Direct 0.9 mg/dL; Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. (Note: RPR/VDRL, HIV 1/2, and Hepatitis A/B/C serologies were not included in the provided test data).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the elevated Alkaline Phosphatase and ultrasound findings of thickened bile ducts, do you have a history of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) or have you ever undergone a colonoscopy that might have been performed for your ulcerative colitis? Additionally, have you experienced any right upper quadrant abdominal pain or fever?

REQUEST TEST: IgG4 levels, Anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA), and Fecal Calprotectin.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: IgG4 levels: Not provided in data; Anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA): Negative (from previous data); Fecal Calprotectin: Not provided in data; MRCP: Not provided in data. NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC). Given your history of ulcerative colitis, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and the ultrasound showing bile duct thickening, PSC is the most likely diagnosis. The negative AMA and lack of IgG4 elevation help rule out Primary Biliary Cholangitis and Autoimmune Pancreatitis, respectively. We can confirm this with the MRCP findings, but clinical presentation strongly supports this conclusion.
